longest_story.title: Just a Guy Named Joe!
longest_story.first_line: Our mildly terrific tale opens in a crowded neighborhood gym, where we find a not-overly-bright habitue named Joe Smith indulging himself in one of his ever-present day-dreams--
longest_story.characters: J. Jonah Jameson; Ned Leeds; Aunt May; Harry Osborn; Joe Smith (villain) (First appearance); Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Gwen Stacy; Flash Thompson; Mary Jane Watson (Only in shadows)
longest_story.synopsis: Average Joe, Joe Smith, fails at being a fighter and tries his hand at acting. Dressed up as a robotic monster, he is zapped with electricity and chemicals which causes him to go on a violent spree against those who doubted his abilities. Meanwhile, Norman Osborn puts a price on Spider-Man’s head and our hero is plagued with goons trying to bump him off. Pete narrowly misses meeting Mary Jane.
longest_story.notes: Steve Ditko's last Spider-Man story. Ditko reportedly turned in his last art for Marvel the last week of November 1965.

longest_story.title: How Green Was My Goblin!
longest_story.inks: Mike Esposito (credited as Mickey Demeo); John Romita (credited as Johnny Romita) (touch-ups)
longest_story.first_line: By now, that web-crawling weasel must have forgotten all about the Green Goblin!
longest_story.characters: Green Goblin [Norman Osborn] (villain) (identity revealed); J. Jonah Jameson; Ned Leeds; Aunt May; Harry Osborn; Spider-Man [Peter Parker]; Gwen Stacy; Mendel Stromm (flashback) (cameo); Flash Thompson; Anna Watson
longest_story.synopsis: Peter heads to the doctor with the sniffles and learns that Aunt May's health is very fragile. Spider-Man is roped into tangling with a bunch of goons who zap him with a mysterious gas. Not realizing that the gas has weakened his spider sense, he changes into Peter Parker under the watchful gaze of the Green Goblin. The Goblin confronts Spidey outside of his home and captures him as Peter is worried that Aunt May might be overcome by the commotion. Trussed up in the Goblin's lair, Peter is shocked when the Goblin takes off his mask and reveals himself to be Norman Osborn.
longest_story.notes: Continued next issue. John Romita touch-up credits from John Romita at the San Diego Comic-Con (July 21, 2006).

longest_story.notes:
In an interview in the fanzine The Web-Spinner (1966) John Romita explained that Bill Ward pencilled a few pages due to deadlines. Nick Caputo suspects he assisted on pgs 13-17. For a more detailed account go to Nick's blog:

http://nick-caputo.blogspot.com/2015/03/john-romitas-first-fanzine-interview.html

Rhino appears in the next two issues. Inking alterations info per John Romita at the San Diego Comic-Con (July 21, 2006).

longest_story.title: Spider-Man No More!
longest_story.first_line: What say we skip any long introductions?
longest_story.characters: Betty Brant; The Burglar (flashback) (cameo); Johnny Carson (cameo); J. Jonah Jameson; Kingpin [Wilson Fisk] (villain) (First appearance); Aunt May; Ed McMahon (cameo); Harry Osborn; Uncle Ben Parker (flashback) (cameo); Patch [Frederick Foswell]; Spider-Man [Peter Parker] (flashback, origin); Gwen Stacy; Dr. Miles Warren; Anna Watson; Mary Jane Watson; The Mob (villain)
longest_story.synopsis: Fearing for his aunt's health and tired of being hounded by Jameson, Peter gives up being Spider-Man and concentrates on being a simple college student. A kid finds the discarded Spider-Man suit in the trash can and brings it to the Daily Bugle where Jonah proudly puts it on display. Peter’s personal life starts looking up but crime increases as the Kingpin gathers the mob under his leadership. Feeling guilty about the crime wave, Peter remembers the lessons taught to him by his uncle's death and decides to become Spider-Man once again.
longest_story.notes: Continued in the next 2 issues. Mike Esposito's alias Mickey Demeo was misspelled as Dimeo in this issue.
